findings.namedBuyers: Verified planning/administrative contacts: Sara Whitwell, Operations Manager; Kevin Rupy, Event Coordination co-chair; Luke Taylor, Association Administration; Stacy Graham and Jaime Zetterstrom, Marketing and Events co-chairs. Sara and Kevin are the preferred first two paths. No source identifies a Toronto accommodation contract signatory or named TD hotel buyer.
findings.futureEdition: Official detailed event page and venue listing publish 26–28 April 2027, including Monday 26 welcome reception, Tuesday 27 full programme/evening networking, Wednesday 28 full programme. However, the official /events/ listing and CFCA social posts publish 27–29 April 2027. Neither source supplies a change notice resolving the discrepancy. Prefer the detailed activity schedule for planning discussion, but do not treat either range as conflict-free; verified overview dates remain null pending organizer confirmation.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications and published downtown venue: pursue a partial delegate/speaker/VIP lodging allocation, not the main conference or exclusive housing. A modest subset within the hotel’s stated 15–109 peak-room target could be suitable, but that is a sales targeting range, NOT event demand. Attendance, nonlocal share, peak rooms and room nights are unpublished. The event is a downtown corporate-office programme, not a resort requirement. No evidence establishes it as too large or too small for this 157-room hotel. The hotel brand states “Restaurant and Lounge closed until further notice”; do not promise dinners, receptions or catering without separate operational confirmation.
findings.venueCommitments: Published Toronto venue: TD Bank at TD Terrace, 160 Front St W, Toronto, Ontario M5J 0G4, Canada. This is Toronto proper, downtown/Financial District, within the hotel’s downtown territory—not an outlying resort, MTCC or Exhibition Place booking. TD Bank is the host and office venue, not an identified housing buyer. This establishes an announced venue, not access to its contract.
findings.historicalRotation: Nine documented predecessor Educational Events rotate through Pittsburgh, London and Washington in 2024; Tucson, Prague and East Brunswick in 2025; Charlotte, Stockholm and Saint Paul in 2026. Both hotel/resort and corporate-office venues occur. CFCA announced the Engage rebrand and four annual in-person events for 2027. This is series recurrence, not proof of annual Toronto recurrence or a 2028 Toronto return.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Toronto 2027: unknown. Edition page names NO hotels and supplies no room block, accommodation booking code/link, housing bureau, RFP, allotment, rate or cutoff. Its relevant section is headed “Travel Logistics. Airports”, and it says the event is “hosted by TD Bank” at TD Terrace; these are travel/venue statements, not lodging commitments. Historical CFCA practice ranges from held hotel rooms (Tucson 2025) and secured overflow (Pittsburgh 2024) to corporate-office events with nearby suggestions. None proves Toronto inventory is open.
findings.organizationStructure: Owner/organizer is the Communications Fraud Control Association (CFCA), a not-for-profit 501(c)(6) international association for communications fraud/risk professionals—not a professional event-planner membership association. Lateral Alliances provides association administration and event management support. TD Bank hosts the Toronto edition at its offices. No separately appointed Toronto PCO, DMC or housing bureau is identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The main meeting venue is already announced at TD offices, so a conference relocation pitch is not supported. No Toronto incumbent hotel, sold-out hotel, overflow shortage or exclusivity is published. Pittsburgh’s April 2024 sold-out Wednesday and secured Hyatt House alternative are historical overflow evidence only, not Toronto evidence. Radisson’s restaurant/lounge closure constrains unverified F&B offers.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Sara Whitwell via the published association mailbox fraud@cfca.org, requesting introduction to the Toronto lodging decision-maker; copy/escalate to Kevin Rupy through CFCA rather than inventing his email. First reconcile 26–28 versus 27–29 April, then ask whether TD/CFCA has contracted accommodation or a housing agent, who signs, hotel names/allotments, nonlocal attendance, peak rooms and pickup nights. If procurement permits, offer a nonexclusive delegate/speaker lodging proposal sized to verified demand. Do not displace TD’s committed meeting venue or offer catered functions until hotel operations approves. Use Luke Taylor as the published named administrative alternative.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 is a confirmed announced Toronto edition, but hotel procurement access is unconfirmed. Lodging inquiry is commercially plausible, not a qualified open RFP or demonstrated overflow requirement. Published dates conflict. No evidence proves accommodation is committed elsewhere, and silence does not prove it is open.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: develop the CFCA/Lateral Alliances relationship now for permitted 2027 lodging and future destination decisions. The documented rotating series supports relationship-development potential, not a guaranteed Toronto repeat. No 2028 Toronto edition was located; do not create dates or local demand for it.
